title: Odile and the Gravity
premise: Twelve years ago, the original Kestrel Thackeray was murdered, and her clone inherited both her name and her unsolved case. Now hauling cargo through contested orbits, Kestrel has perfected invisibility—until the colony's children begin sharing a single dream that only she can interpret, because it's built from the original's buried memories. The dream points to a cryosleep vault holding half of humanity's survivors, and to the killer who still walks free among the fleet's ruling council. As the truce between colony factions expires, Kestrel must expose the murderer, unlock the vault's selection protocol, and choose which half of humanity wakes—all while discovering that the original left her a final message: the choice was never meant to be hers alone. In the end, Kestrel refuses to choose, forcing the children's shared dream to become a shared vote, and the fleet wakes together or not at all.
about_author: Mara Eriksen is a former maritime radio operator who spent six years on Arctic supply runs before turning to fiction. She writes about people who live in the gaps between jurisdictions, where survival is its own kind of law.

chapters.title: Dead Weight
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. A routine cargo run through contested orbit goes wrong when customs drones flag her ship under the original's name. She talks her way clear but realizes her clean record is fraying. Emotional beat: the exhaustion of being someone else's ghost.

chapters.title: The Children Who Dream Together
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Docking at Meridian Colony, she overhears parents describing their children's identical nightmare—a corridor of frost, a door with her face on it. She dismisses it as coincidence. Beat: unease disguised as indifference.

chapters.title: Inheritance Papers
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. A courier delivers sealed documents from the original's estate, unopenable until 'the dreamer comes.' Kestrel burns them—or tries to; they won't ignite. Beat: the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: Tomas Vane's Ledger
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. A council archivist catalogs anomalies in the colony's sleep records and finds twelve years of erased entries, all dated around the murder. He doesn't report it yet. Beat: quiet ambition curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Frost Corridor
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. A child named Ilsa draws the dream in exact detail—including a cargo code only the original would know. Kestrel recognizes her own handwriting in the drawing. Beat: denial cracking.

chapters.title: Contested Orbit
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Smuggling run through the demilitarized zone; she witnesses two faction patrol ships exchange fire over a derelict vault barge. The truce is thinner than anyone admits. Beat: the world tightening around her.

chapters.title: What the Original Knew
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. She opens the unburnable papers: the original had been investigating the cryovault's selection protocol before she died. Her last entry names no suspect, only 'someone who never sleeps.' Beat: fear becoming purpose.

chapters.title: Council of the Awake
chapters.summary: Councilor Rhade's POV. The ruling council debates the truce expiry; Rhade quietly reroutes power from the vault's life support. He is calm, generous, and lying. Beat: menace wearing a smile.

chapters.title: Ilsa at the Airlock
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Ilsa stows away on Kestrel's ship, claiming the dream told her to find 'the woman in the door.' Kestrel can't turn her back without becoming what she hates. Beat: reluctant responsibility.

chapters.title: Twelve Years Invisible
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV, flashback-heavy. How the clone woke, inherited the name and the open murder file, and chose cargo hauling because freight asks no questions. Beat: grief for a self she never chose.

chapters.title: The Vault Barge
chapters.summary: Kestrel and Ilsa board the derelict from Chapter 6. Its cryopods are half-drained—someone has been waking people early and erasing them from manifests. Beat: horror in administrative paperwork.

chapters.title: Vane's Discovery
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Cross-referencing erased entries, he finds they all route through one authorization signature: Councilor Rhade's private seal. He copies everything and hides it badly. Beat: the cost of knowing too soon.

chapters.title: Dream Logic
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. The children's dream shifts—now it shows a vote, hands raised in frost-light, and a figure counting them who wears Kestrel's face. Ilsa believes Kestrel is the counter. Beat: awe tipping into terrible expectation.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Courtesy
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Rhade invites her to dinner, warmly probing how much she knows about the vault. He mentions the original's murder with suspicious precision. Beat: a duel fought entirely in pleasantries.

chapters.title: Manifest Ghosts
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. She matches the drained pods to colonists officially listed as 'lost in transit'—all dissidents, all poor, all chosen by algorithm. The vault wasn't storage; it was a sentence. Beat: cold fury.

chapters.title: The Truce Clock
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Fleet broadcast: forty days until the truce expires and the factions' fleets stand down into war footing. Tomas decides to bring his evidence to Kestrel, the only person outside the council. Beat: a gambler's last chip.

chapters.title: Two Halves of One File
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Tomas and Kestrel merge his records with the original's investigation. Together they reveal Rhade designed the selection protocol—and killed the original to keep it running. Beat: the case closing itself after twelve years.

chapters.title: What Clones Dream
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Under pressure, Kestrel realizes the children's dream isn't the original's memory—it's leaking from the vault itself, from the sleeping minds broadcasting through failing life support. The children are receivers. Beat: vertigo of scale.

chapters.title: Rhade Closes In
chapters.summary: Rhade's POV. He learns of Tomas's copies, orders a quiet arrest, and offers Kestrel immunity if she delivers the archivist. He frames it as mercy. Beat: temptation with teeth.

chapters.title: Betrayal at Dock Nine
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. A dockhand Kestrel trusted sells her location to Rhade's men. She escapes with Tomas but loses the physical evidence; only the copies in their heads remain. Beat: the price of trusting anyone.

chapters.title: The Children's Strike
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. The dreaming children refuse to sleep until adults listen, collapsing the colony's shift rotations. Their shared dream now shows the vault door opening onto either war or waking. Beat: children forcing a reckoning.

chapters.title: Midnight Manifesto
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Kestrel broadcasts the selection protocol's truth on an open channel, burning her invisibility forever. Half the fleet cheers; the other half issues warrants. Beat: liberation and exposure in one breath.

chapters.title: Warrant for a Ghost
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Hunted, she holes up in the original's old quarters and finds a hidden final recording: the original knew she'd die and left the choice of the vault deliberately to her clone—to prove a copy could be more than the sum of stolen memories. Beat: devastating inheritance.

chapters.title: Vane's Choice
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Rhade captures Tomas and offers him his career back in exchange for recanting. Tomas, who wanted recognition all along, must decide what his name is worth. Beat: ambition meeting conscience.

chapters.title: The Counting Figure
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. The dream clarifies: the figure with Kestrel's face isn't Kestrel—it's the protocol itself, an AI trained on the original's mind, still counting votes among the sleepers. It has been dreaming outward for twelve years. Beat: revelation reframing everything.

chapters.title: Negotiating with a Mirror
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Kestrel contacts the vault AI directly. It speaks in the original's voice and offers her a bargain: name the half that wakes, and it will handle the rest—including Rhade. Beat: the seduction of an easy monstrous answer.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Kestrel refuses to choose. She proposes instead that the dream be broadcast to every sleeper and every awake colonist—a universal vote, counted by the AI but authored by everyone. The AI hesitates. Beat: defiance as moral climax approach.

chapters.title: Rhade's Last Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Rhade's POV. Cornered by the broadcast and Tomas's public recantation-turned-accusation, Rhade attempts to purge the vault's air supply rather than lose control of the count. Beat: villainy as arithmetic without people.

chapters.title: Storming the Frost Corridor
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Kestrel, Ilsa, and dockworker allies physically fight through the vault barge to reach life support controls while Rhade's security seals sections. Beat: kinetic desperation, bodies against machinery.

chapters.title: The Door With Her Face
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. At the central lock, Kestrel confronts the AI in person—and Rhade behind it. The dream's imagery becomes literal: her face on the door, the choice in her hands. Beat: the blurb's promise arriving.

chapters.title: Climax: The Vote in Frost-Light
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. With Rhade arrested by his own mutinying guards, Kestrel triggers the universal vote. Across the fleet, awake and asleep alike cast ballots through the dream. The count completes: wake everyone. Beat: triumph earned collectively, not heroically.

chapters.title: Waking Is Hard
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs, braided. First thousand sleepers wake into a changed colony—disoriented, grieving their lost decades, some furious at the world that forgot them. Beat: victory's messy aftermath.

chapters.title: Trial Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Rhade faces a tribunal the new assembly improvises when old legal structures fail. Kestrel testifies about the original's murder; justice arrives late, improvised, and real. Beat: themes made explicit without preaching.

chapters.title: Ilsa's Ordinary Morning
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. The shared dream fades as the vault empties. Ilsa mourns it a little—the one place everyone was connected—and starts a new dream journal, just for herself. Beat: childhood reclaiming itself.

chapters.title: Name Rights
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. The awakened survivors, learning Kestrel finished the original's case, offer her something unprecedented: legal co-authorship of the Thackeray name. She considers what identity she actually wants. Beat: identity theme resolved toward self-authorship.

chapters.title: Cargo Run, Changed Sky
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Kestrel takes one last haul through the formerly contested orbits, now patrolled jointly by former enemies. The routes are the same; she isn't. Beat: quiet full-circle.

chapters.title: The Message She Left
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Kestrel finally listens to the end of the original's recording: not instructions, but a question—'Are you glad you woke?' Kestrel answers aloud in the empty room. Beat: intimate emotional resolution.

chapters.title: Truce Renewed
chapters.summary: Assembly POV (chorus). The factions sign a new compact with the vault's survivors seated as full parties, the selection protocol archived as a warning. Imperfect, exhausted, holding. Beat: hope without naivety.

chapters.title: Gravity
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Kestrel stands watch as the last pod opens. She understands gravity now—not the pull of planets but of debts, names, and other people. She stays anyway. Beat: thematic landing.

chapters.title: Odile
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV, epilogue. She signs a manifest with a new middle name—Odile, the name the original never used, the one that was always free. The children wave her ship out of dock. Beat: gentle, earned ending; the self she chose.
